thread:
Priya: Heads-up 0-min wargame tomorrow 11:00PT to finalize competitive hooks for launch. Goal: 2 defensible benchmark callouts, 3 SDR hooks, 1 rebut slide. Who's in? :crossed_swords:
Dylan: I'll join. Bringing latency vs managed APIs and a short note on routing policies.
Hannah: In. Uploading P50/P95 for chat at 256/512 tokens and canary bench CSVs.
Omar: I'll draft a compact competitor matrix: where they win vs where we win.
Riley: SDR hooks should be punchy. Suggest 3 flavors: PLG, AE, Infra-tech (<=20 words).
Priya: Draft hooks to iterate:
  PLG: "Cut token spend and keep latency predictable across hosted, dedicated, and private."
  AE: "SLA-backed inference with private deployment options  production-ready."
  Infra-tech: "Automatic batching + KV caching + quant-friendly kernels = lower unit cost w/out latency tradeoffs."
Dylan: Bench language: avoid absolutes. Use qualifiers and link appendix. e.g., "Up to 4x lower unit cost in our benchmark under typical chat loads".
Hannah: Note: our staging 512-run medians: Redwood ~20ms, CloudX ~110ms on a similar GPU. Cost multipliers vary by quant & batch. I'll attach raw logs.
Omar: Rebut matrix should cover: "We already use CloudX", "We need enterprise SLA", "We can't host private infra". Two-line rebut each.
Riley: Example rebut for "We already use CloudX": "They offer scale; we lower per-token spend via batching/caching and provide a migration path to dedicated/private with consistent ops."
Priya: Inbound routing: if demo request contains latency|SLA|private|dedicated|throughput|predictable -> tag enterprise-sales, else growth-inbound. SRD ops to implement.
launch-bot: Calendar invite sent for 11:00-11:50 PT to #marketing.
Dylan: Action items: Hannah -> bench appendix + CSVs; Omar -> competitor/rebut slide; Riley -> 3 SDR hooks + A/B variants; Priya -> stitch pre-read and run wargame.
Priya: Keep claims conservative and link to appendix. We'll finalize post-wargame and push a one-pager to SDRs on Friday. :thumbsup:
